Subject: Model fit evals - Redwood benchmarks & next steps

Hi Sara — great to meet yesterday. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery call so the broader BrightAI team has a single reference: 

Summary of fit
- Primary goal: real-time chat generation for customer support triage with 2–3s end-to-end SLA and sub-$0.002/token unit cost target on peak volumes.
- Data sensitivity: PII in transcripts, must be isolated (VPC) for production.

Recommended models & config (initial)- Redwood-4-13B (int8, KV cache enabled) — good quality/cost balance for short-context responses (p50 latency ~120ms, p95 ~420ms on p4d.24xlarge).
- Llama-2-Chat-70B (Q4_0 quant) — higher quality for tricky CX intents; expect p50 ~280ms, p95 ~750ms on same hardware; reserve for high-value flows.
- Autoscaling policy: target 80% CPU/GPU utilization, burst to reserved capacity for spikes.

Attached: redwood_benchmarks_brightai_20260302.csv (sample evals), prompt_set_brightai_v1.txt (our suggested prompt sets and edge cases). Also sharing the Redwood-verified perf profile pages with latency percentiles and TPS numbers: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/brightai-v1

Immediate next steps
1) Ill upload a short benchmark run for your sample prompt set and share results by EOD tomorrow.
2) If the numbers look good, propose a 2-week pilot (mutual action plan attached) with a small reserved pool and access to the Redwood console.
3) Onboarding call: do you have 30 minutes on Wednesday or Thursday?

Open questions from our side
- Typical peak concurrent sessions and expected avg tokens per response? (short estimate is fine)
- Who should be in for security intake (SOC 2 / VPC onboarding)?

Thanks — Ill run the sample evals and send links.

— Alex

Thanks Alex — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications before we dig into the CSV: 

- For the Llama-2-Chat-70B numbers, are those for 1-shot prompts or multi-turns with a growing context? Our transcripts often go 8–10 turns and we care about tail latency as threads grow.
- On quality regressions: do you surface regression alerts against a baseline prompt set? Weve seen drift cause subtle behavior changes and want to avoid regressions hitting prod.

Were generally interested in the 2-week pilot. Ill loop in legal for basic T&Cs once we have a mutual action plan.

— Sara
Sara Klein | Head of Data Products, BrightAI
sara.klein@brightai.com
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>
To: Sara Klein <sara.klein@brightai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model fit evals - Redwood benchmarks & next steps

Thanks Sara — great questions. Responding inline: 

- Long-context / multi-turn latency: the Llama-2-Chat-70B numbers I shared are for a 1-shot + 256-token response baseline. With growing context we rely on KV-cache and our selective kernel paths; typical impact is +10–30% latency for 8–10 turns depending on prompt length. Tail percentiles (p95/p99) increase more for long context, which is why we recommend routing high-value multi-turns to the 70B variant and using Redwood-4-13B for short flows.

- Quality regression monitoring: yes — Redwood Optimize can run continuous evals against your canonical prompt set and emit regression alerts tied to specific model versions and quantization profiles. We store evaluation diffs (text similarity + business metric proxies) and will alert if agreement drops below a threshold you set. We can also gate rollouts with canaries and automatic fallback to the baseline model.

Ive uploaded the detailed CSV and a short perf dashboard snapshot to the shared link: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/brightai-v1 (see the "detailed-run-20260302" tab). The attached MAP_BrightAI_20260302.pdf is a one-page mutual action plan that outlines responsibilities, timelines, and milestone success criteria for the 2-week pilot.

Proposed pilot milestones
- Day 0-2: onboarding + connect logs/keys (security intake).
- Day 3-7: smoke benchmarks on your sample prompt set (we run both Redwood-4-13B and Llama-2-Chat-70B).
- Day 8-14: evaluation window + regression checks, iterate prompts and routing.

If that sounds good Ill get calendar invites out. Also: for the security intake please cc security@brightai.com and your SOC2 contact so we can share the evidence package.

— Alex
